title: Systematics, multi-gene phylogeny, reassignment, and redefinition of the family Hemicycliostylidae with a rod-shaped structure in the pharynx (Protista: Ciliophora)
content:
Abstract
Hypotrichous ciliates have long faced persistent taxonomic and systematic challenges owing to their morphological diversification and extensive polymorphism. This study provides a systematic revision of the family Hemicycliostylidae using an integrative approach that includes morphological and ontogenetic data, in addition to multigene phylogenetic evidence from SSU rDNA, ITS1–5.8S–ITS2, LSU rDNA, and a concatenated dataset. The study proposes the following results: (i) the paroral and endoral in Anteaustralocirrus pattern, cortical granules elliptical to rod-shaped, and heritable rod-shaped structure in the pharynx with environmentally regulated phenotypic plasticity as diagnostic morphological synapomorphies for Hemicycliostylidae; (ii) a comprehensive revision of the diagnosis for the family Hemicycliostylidae to define its morphological synapomorphies better; (iii) the establishment of Paraaustralothrix gen. nov. to accommodate species previously assigned to Australothrix, in addition to having paroral and endoral in Oxytricha pattern; and (iv) stochastic mapping of representative morphological characters onto the phylogeny to infer the evolutionary pathways of Hemicycliostylidae genera/species and Paraaustralothrix gen. nov.
siteTitle: Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society Current Issue
